title: Migration Gateway + Compatibility Sentinel for Toolcall/Streaming Schema Evolution
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We are rolling out schema changes and behavioral updates for streaming responses and tool/function calling to enable structured, typed outputs and more predictable fallbacks. Past migrations exposed two recurring risks: 1) silent contract drift for streaming/message-fragmented tool calls, and 2) clients getting unexpected structured-output shapes when behavior flags flip. Teams need a prescriptive migration surface that validates live traffic and provides unobtrusive rollbacks and signals for client owners.
problem_statement: Current deprecation runs rely on offline compatibility tests and ad-hoc shadow runs. This leaves gaps for multipart stream delivery and toolcalls that only manifest under production load (prefix caching, KV reuse, partial tool emissions). We need a runtime guard and a migration kit that observes, validates, and optionally rejects or rewrites requests to maintain contract fidelity while enabling incremental client upgrades.
proposal_summary: Introduce a Migration Gateway and Compatibility Sentinel: the gateway is a controllable interception layer that can shadow-validate or mute new schema features for selected client cohorts; the sentinel is a telemetry + policy engine that enforces soft or hard compatibility decisions (warn, reject, auto-rewrite). This pair enables: staged opt-ins, live contract linting for streamed fragments, deterministic replay for failing cases, and a rollout leash to automatically pause deprecations for high-severity regressions.
non_goals: We will not implement a full client-side SDK orchestration in this ticket. Language-specific client libraries that consume the migration signals are out of scope. Deep model-level changes (architecture/weights) are also out of scope for this work.
acceptance_criteria: Migration Gateway can be toggled per-customer and per-route via Console feature flags
Sentinel implements three policy modes: observe (telemetry only), soft-block (warn + attach mismatch metadata), hard-block (reject with migration hint), and mode can be changed without rollout
Shadow validation supports streaming fragments: it reassembles fragments server-side and runs schema conformance checks in the same execution context as production responses
End-to-end regression tests included: replay harness that replays historical traffic and asserts parity metrics (token-level diffs, toolcall timing and tool invocation counts)
Migration guidance doc and a migration-template spec (example prompts, sample client errors, rollback steps) published to Confluence/Drive
Telemetry captures a compact compatibility event for each evaluated request with fields: route, model, snapshot_version, validation_status, policy_action, client_id (hashed), and regression_score
An incident playbook for high-severity regressions is linked in the migration doc and the Console surface surfaces the sentinel's top 10 recent rejects and examples
rollout_plan: 1) Implement Gateway + Sentinel backend + minimal Console toggles behind a runtime flag (internal-only rollout)
2) Run internal shadow validation on staging traffic for 2 weeks, collect false-positive/negative matrix
3) Enable observe mode for a small set of opt-in customers (developer beta) and gather client feedback
4) Expand soft-block to a larger cohort with automatic enriched telemetry (replay ids) for failing requests
5) If stability targets met, release hard-block as opt-in for an internal team; keep migration docs and SDK recipes published
6) Full release: make Gateway toggles available in Console and start recommended retirement windows for legacy flags
testing_plan: unit tests for sentinel policy evaluation rules
integration tests for gateway toggle behavior across dedicated/private modes
end-to-end replay harness that compares production response traces with shadow-validated traces
fuzz targets for fragmented streaming reassembly and schema linter
security_considerations: Gateway will redact PII before any shadow validation telemetry and only store client_id as a hashed identifier. Access to sentinel events will be RBAC-controlled in Console. No customer plaintext data will be exported in migration reports.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoffs considered: doing full hard-stops at API boundary vs. soft monitoring. We default to soft mechanisms to avoid customer disruption; hard-block is gated and opt-in. Reassembling streaming fragments server-side has CPU and memory cost — initial rollout will use sampling and size limits. We will prioritize routes with the highest regression risk (tool invocation surfaces and structured-output endpoints).
next_steps: Align ENG owners for runtime and replay harness (ask ENG leads to assign tickets)
Prepare migration-template doc and quickstart scripts for customers
Schedule 1:1 with Solutions engineering for early adopters
Add sentinel metrics to Console alpha dashboard
